# Analyze differences in metBMI and measured BMI between the antibiotic use groups
In our metabolite regression, we see that antibiotic use may have a mixed effect 
on the blood metabolome. 
- Namely, there are some metabolites that are negatively
associated with metS (for example, cinnamoylglycine), and antibiotic users tend
to have less of this metabolite in their blood compared to non-users. 
- On the other hand, metabolites such as 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate are **positively** associated
with metS while being **negatively** associated with recent antibiotic use. 

## Read in data

```{r libraries}
library(ggplot2)     
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(data.table)
library(cowplot)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggeffects)
library(car)
```

Read data from Lance. Looks like the leading zero was dropped so we'll have to 
add that back in.

```{r read.data}
# metBMI data from Lance
metBMIs = read.csv("../data/metBMI_for_ids_crystal_test.csv", 
                   colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

# Add leading 0s
#metBMIs$public_client_id <- paste0("0", metBMIs$public_client_id)
# sum(is.na(metBMIs$bBMI))

# Read in metadata and alpha diversities
metadata = read.csv("../data/metabolites_merged_used_for_regressions.csv",
                    colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))[, 1:27]

# Factor categorical vars
metadata$sex <- factor(metadata$sex)
metadata$meds_blood_sugar <- factor(metadata$meds_blood_sugar)
metadata$meds_cholesterol <- factor(metadata$meds_cholesterol)

# Specify levels so plots have correct order
metadata$abx_recency <- factor(metadata$abx_recency,
                                 levels = c("none","twelve","three"))

# For interpretation
metadata$centered_age <- metadata$age - mean(metadata$age)
```

## Initial Visualization

Merge tables and visualize!

```{r merge}
metBMIs_small <- metBMIs[ , c('public_client_id','bBMI')]

# Turn df into data.table for melting later
metBMI_meta <- data.table(
  inner_join(metadata,
             metBMIs_small,
             by = "public_client_id")
  )

table(metBMI_meta$abx_recency)
```

For initial visualization, let's replicate the plot that Lance made but comparing
the results with/without the outliers.

```{r remove.outliers}
# Watanabe et al. removed +/- 3x mean from their models
# Will do the same as outliers will have poor prediction
metBMI_meta_clean <- metBMI_meta %>%
  filter(
    abs(BMI_CALC - mean(BMI_CALC)) <= (3 * sd(BMI_CALC)))

table(metBMI_meta_clean$abx_recency)
```

Finally, plot the agreement between measured and predicted BMI.

```{r save.cleaned, fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
# Axis limits
lims <- range(c(metBMI_meta_clean$bBMI, metBMI_meta_clean$BMI_CALC))

metBMI_meta_clean <- metBMI_meta_clean %>%
  mutate(
    resid_measured_BMI = resid(lm(BMI_CALC ~ sex + centered_age + 
                    meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR +
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + abx_recency, data = .)),
    resid_predict_BMI = resid(lm(bBMI ~ sex + centered_age + 
                    meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR +
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + abx_recency, data = .))
  )

cor_test <- cor.test(metBMI_meta_clean$resid_predict_BMI, 
                     metBMI_meta_clean$resid_measured_BMI,
                     method = "pearson")

cor_test

r <- cor_test$estimate
p <- cor_test$p.value

corr_test_label <- paste0(
  sprintf("Pearson's r = %.4f", r),
  "\nP= ", format.pval(p, digits = 4)
)

corr_metBMI_plot <- ggplot(metBMI_meta_clean, aes(x=bBMI, y=BMI_CALC)) +
  geom_abline(                               # y = x
    slope = 1, intercept = 0, 
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.2, size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se = TRUE) + 
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = Inf,
    y = -Inf,
    label = corr_test_label,
    hjust = 1.1,
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 6
  ) + 
  coord_equal(xlim = lims, ylim = lims) +
  labs(x = "Predicted BMI (metBMI, kg/m²)", y = "Measured BMI (kg/m²)") +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray80", linewidth = 0.1),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18), 
    axis.text = element_text(size = 18)
  )

corr_metBMI_plot
```

```{r save.corr.plot}
# Save plot
pdf("../figures/abx_recency_metBMI_pearson_r.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)  # open a PDF device
plot(corr_metBMI_plot)
dev.off()
```

# Add metabolite associations
 
Check to see if the error is associated with more or less of certain metabolites.
Pick abx responsive metabolites that are robustly maintained in the metBMI model 
(suppl table metBMI).
 
## First let's read in the metabolomics data

```{r read.in.metab.data}
# We will calculate the difference and center that error
metBMI_meta_clean$delta_measure = metBMI_meta_clean$bBMI - metBMI_meta_clean$BMI_CALC
metBMI_meta_clean$centered_error = (metBMI_meta_clean$delta_measure - mean(metBMI_meta_clean$delta_measure))

# Read in data
metabs = read.csv('../data/metabolites_merged_used_for_regressions.csv', 
                   colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

metabs_subset <- metabs[, c('public_client_id', 'metabolite_100001083', 'metabolite_240')]

metbmi_metabolites <- inner_join(
  metBMI_meta_clean,
  metabs_subset,
  by = "public_client_id")
```

# Onto statistical testing

## Testing differences in measured and predicted BMI by abx group

### BMI_CALC
We know that the measured BMI between our antibiotic use recency groups differ,
let's re-examine this below.

```{r individual.models.BMI_CALC}
bmi_calc_model <- lm(BMI_CALC ~ sex + centered_age + 
                    meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR +
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + abx_recency, data=metBMI_meta_clean)
summary(bmi_calc_model)
```

Yep, the BMI of individuals in the abx_recency groups are ~1 kg/m^2 larger than
that of the "none" group.

### metBMI

```{r}
bbmi_model <- lm(bBMI ~  sex + centered_age +
                    meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR +
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + abx_recency, data=metBMI_meta_clean)
summary(bbmi_model)
```
Similarly, the metBMI of the antibiotic use recency groups is also larger. 

# Okie dokie, let's move onto clinical chems

```{r merge.labs}
labs_clean = read.csv("../data/clincal_chems_abx_users_clean.csv", 
                   colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

# Grab only the lab cols
labs_list <- colnames(labs_clean %>% dplyr::select(-(1:31)))
labs_clean$vendor <- factor(labs_clean$vendor)

labs_clean$season <- factor(labs_clean$season)
labs_small_df <- labs_clean[, c("public_client_id", "vendor", labs_list)] 

# Merge
metBMI_labs <- data.table(inner_join(metBMI_meta_clean,
             labs_small_df,
             by = "public_client_id"))
```

Vectorize running models:

```{r vec.models.both.vendors}
# Check levels abx
levels(metBMI_labs$abx_recency)

# Run models
lab_models_all <- setNames(lapply(chem_outcomes, function(outcome) {
    # Drop NAs for this specific outcome
    subdat <- metBMI_labs[!is.na(metBMI_labs[[outcome]]), ]
    
    # Build formula dynamically
    form <- as.formula(
      paste(outcome, "~ sex + centered_age + centered_eGFR +
                    meds_cholesterol + meds_blood_sugar + 
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_BMI + vendor +
                    centered_error * abx_recency + 
                    centered_BMI:abx_recency + centered_BMI:centered_error"))
    
    mod <- lm(form, data = subdat)   # Run model
    attr(mod, "outcome") <- outcome  # Attach outcome name to the model
    mod                              # Return the model object
  }), 
  
  chem_outcomes) 
```

## Concatenate and run type II ANOVA:
Here looking for the term-wide significance of the `abx_recency:error` interaction 
term.

```{r}
extract_omni <- function(mod_list) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(mod_list), function(nm) {
    av  <- Anova(mod_list[[nm]], type = "II")
    row <- "centered_error:abx_recency"
    data.frame(
      outcome = nm,
      n_subjects = nobs(mod_list[[nm]]),
      F_val  = if (row %in% rownames(av)) av[row, "F value"] else NA_real_,
      df_num = if (row %in% rownames(av)) av[row, "Df"]      else NA_integer_,
      p_omni = if (row %in% rownames(av)) av[row, "Pr(>F)"]  else NA_real_,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

omni_all <- rbind(extract_omni(lab_models_all), extract_omni(lab_models_one_vendor))
omni_all$q_omni <- p.adjust(omni_all$p_omni, method = "fdr")
```

Let's print the chems with an interaction meeting our threshold:
```{r show.significant.chems}
omni_all %>% filter(omni_all$q_omni <0.1)
```

## Awesome, after running models, let's extract covariates

```{r lm.results.both.vendors}
terms_of_interest <- c("centered_error:abx_recencythree",
                       "centered_error:abx_recencytwelve")

# Here global model refers to covars used through the rest of the paper
# Later I will have to do sens analysis for the vitd supplmentation and season
abx_term_results_global_model <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(lab_models_all), function(outcome_name) {
  
  mod <- lab_models_all[[outcome_name]]
  coef_table <- summary(mod)$coefficients
  
  available_terms <- intersect(terms_of_interest, rownames(coef_table))
  
  if (length(available_terms) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  data.frame(
    outcome = outcome_name,
    term = available_terms,
    estimate = round(coef_table[available_terms, "Estimate"], 4),
    std_error = round(coef_table[available_terms, "Std. Error"], 4),
    statistic = coef_table[available_terms, "t value"],
    p_value = coef_table[available_terms, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
```

Next move onto those supplied by one one vendor.

```{r lm.results.one.vendor}
abx_term_results_global_one_vendor <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(lab_models_one_vendor), function(outcome_name) {
  
  mod <- lab_models_one_vendor[[outcome_name]]
  coef_table <- summary(mod)$coefficients
  
  available_terms <- intersect(terms_of_interest, rownames(coef_table))
  
  if (length(available_terms) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  data.frame(
    outcome = outcome_name,
    term = available_terms,
    estimate = round(coef_table[available_terms, "Estimate"], 4),
    std_error = round(coef_table[available_terms, "Std. Error"], 4),
    statistic = coef_table[available_terms, "t value"],
    p_value = coef_table[available_terms, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
```

After extracting the terms, let's bind the rows and perform FDR correction. 

```{r bind.results.FDR}
# Add the number of participants observed per reg model
n_map <- sapply(lab_models_all, nobs)
abx_term_results_global_model$n_subjects <-
  unname(n_map[abx_term_results_global_model$outcome])

# Redefine for one vendor
n_map <- sapply(lab_models_one_vendor, nobs)
abx_term_results_global_one_vendor$n_subjects <-
  unname(n_map[abx_term_results_global_one_vendor$outcome])

# Bind data
lab_reg_results_all <- rbind(abx_term_results_global_model, abx_term_results_global_one_vendor)

# FDR correction
lab_reg_results_all$fdr_p_value <- round(
  ave(
  lab_reg_results_all$p_value,
  lab_reg_results_all$term,
  FUN = function(p) p.adjust(p, method = "fdr")), 4)
```

Now let's print the rows for those significant in the F-test:
```{r sig.chems.interaction.betas}
get_coefs_list <- omni_all %>% 
  filter(q_omni <0.1) %>% 
  pull(outcome) %>% as.list()

lab_reg_results_all %>% filter(outcome %in% get_coefs_list)
```

## Look at results in greater detail

### Plotting functions
```{r plotting.functions}
abx_colors = c("none" = "#007ea7", "twelve" = "#80ced7", "three" = "darkgrey")

fit_chem <- function(df, chemistry, id_col = "public_client_id") {

  stopifnot(chemistry %in% names(df))

  subdat <- df[!is.na(df[[chemistry]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (id_col %in% names(subdat)) rownames(subdat) <- subdat[[id_col]]

  # vendor is only estimable when >1 level survives the NA filter
  n_vendor <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(subdat$vendor)))
  rhs <- c("sex", "centered_age", "centered_eGFR",
           "meds_cholesterol", "meds_blood_sugar",
           paste0("PC", 1:5), "centered_BMI",
           if (n_vendor > 1) "vendor",
           "centered_error * abx_recency",
           "centered_BMI:abx_recency", "centered_BMI:centered_error")

  form <- as.formula(paste(chemistry, "~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
  mod  <- lm(form, data = subdat)
  mf  <- model.frame(mod) 
  dat <- as.data.frame(subdat)
  stopifnot(nrow(dat) == nrow(mf))   # Make sure data, mod are aligned
  
  list(mod = mod, dat = dat, outcome = chemistry, vendor_adjusted = n_vendor > 1)
}

plot_chem <- function(df, chemistry, y_lab = chemistry, focal = c("centered_error", "abx_recency"),
                      colors = abx_colors, clip = c(.025, .975)) {

  fit <- fit_chem(df, chemistry)
  mod <- fit$mod; dat <- fit$dat
  
  ref_value <- function(x) {
    if (is.numeric(x)) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    else if (is.factor(x)) factor(names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
                                  levels = levels(x))
    else names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
  }

  nuisance <- setdiff(all.vars(formula(mod))[-1], focal)
  refs <- lapply(dat[intersect(nuisance, names(dat))], ref_value)
  refs$centered_BMI <- 0                      # explicit mean-BMI slice

  newdat_ref <- dat
  for (v in names(refs)) newdat_ref[[v]] <- refs[[v]]

  dat$partial_y <- as.numeric(predict(mod, newdata = newdat_ref)) + residuals(mod)

  # pass the SAME reference values to ggpredict so points and lines share an intercept
  cond <- refs[vapply(refs, function(z) is.numeric(z) || is.factor(z), logical(1))]
  cond <- cond[setdiff(names(cond), focal)]

  pred <- ggeffects::ggpredict(
            mod, terms = c("centered_error [all]", "abx_recency"),
            condition = unlist(lapply(cond, function(z)
                          if (is.factor(z)) as.character(z) else z))) |>
    as.data.frame() |> dplyr::rename(centered_error = x, abx_recency = group)

  support <- dat |> dplyr::group_by(abx_recency) |>
    dplyr::summarise(lo = quantile(centered_error, clip[1], na.rm = TRUE),
                     hi = quantile(centered_error, clip[2], na.rm = TRUE),
                     n  = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  pred_clipped <- pred |> dplyr::inner_join(support, by = "abx_recency") |>
    dplyr::filter(centered_error >= lo, centered_error <= hi)

  lab_n <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n = %d)",
       as.character(support$abx_recency), support$n),
      as.character(support$abx_recency))

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = dat, aes(centered_error, partial_y, colour = abx_recency),
        alpha = .15, size = 3) +
    geom_rug(data = dat, aes(x = centered_error, colour = abx_recency), 
             sides = "b", alpha = .5, length = unit(.03, "npc")) +
    geom_ribbon(data = pred_clipped, aes(centered_error, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
                fill = "black", alpha = .3) +
    geom_line(data = pred_clipped, aes(centered_error, predicted),
       colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ abx_recency, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(abx_recency = lab_n)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    #scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(x = "Centered BMI prediction error (metBMI \u2212 BMI)",
         y = paste0(y_lab, "\n(partial residuals, mean BMI)")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  invisible(list(plot = p, mod = mod, dat = dat, pred = pred_clipped,
           support = support, vendor_adjusted = fit$vendor_adjusted))
}
```

# Vitamin D sensitivity analyses

## Check to see if this association is driven by supplement use or seasonality

```{r read.vit.d.data}
vit_d = read.csv('../data/vit_d_info_abx_clients.csv', 
                   colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

metbmi_labs_vitd <- inner_join(
  metBMI_labs,
  vit_d,
  by = "public_client_id")

metbmi_labs_vitd$vitamin_d_flag <- factor(metbmi_labs_vitd$vitamin_d_flag)
metbmi_labs_vitd$season <- factor(metbmi_labs_vitd$season)

levels(metbmi_labs_vitd$vitamin_d_flag)
levels(metbmi_labs_vitd$season)
```

```{r visualize.serum.vitd.supp.use}
ggplot(metbmi_labs_vitd, aes(vitamin_d_flag, VITAMIND_25_OHTOT)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title= "", x = "Vitamin D Supplement Use", y = "VITAMIND_25_OHTOT") +
  facet_wrap(vars(abx_recency))
```

Alright this is really cool! The differences between Vitamin D supplement users
and non-users is pretty apparent. 

Let's rerun our model with the Vitamin D flag added!

```{r run.lab.model.vit.d}
# drop the one missing row to remove warnings
subdat_vit_D <- metbmi_labs_vitd %>%
  filter(!(is.na(VITAMIND_25_OHTOT) | is.na(vitamin_d_flag)))

vit_d_supp_model <- lm(VITAMIND_25_OHTOT ~ sex + centered_age + centered_eGFR +
                         meds_cholesterol + meds_blood_sugar + 
                         PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_BMI + vendor +
                         centered_error * abx_recency + 
                         centered_BMI:abx_recency + centered_BMI:centered_error +
                         season + vitamin_d_flag,
                    data = subdat_vit_D)

car::Anova(vit_d_supp_model, type = "II")
```


```{r save.facet.off}
# pdf("figures/emmip_vitd_three_way_interaction.pdf", width = 6, height = 8)  # open a PDF device
# plot(vit_d_emmip)
# dev.off()
```

There are two large outliers in the model. They have Vit D 25-OH levels of
~150 and ~200. The reference range for both lab vendors is 30-100 ng/mL, and levels
of under <125 ng/mL are considered normal. Reassuringly, these two points are in
the individuals who are taking the vitamin D supplements. However, I should perform
another sensitivity analysis to see if the interaction is still significant after
removing those points. 

```{r remove.vitd.outliers}
subdat_vit_D_clean <- subdat_vit_D[subdat_vit_D$VITAMIND_25_OHTOT < 150]

vit_d_supp_model_clean <- lm(VITAMIND_25_OHTOT ~ sex + centered_age + centered_eGFR +
                         meds_cholesterol + meds_blood_sugar + 
                         PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_BMI + vendor +
                         centered_error * abx_recency + 
                         centered_BMI:abx_recency + centered_BMI:centered_error +
                         season + vitamin_d_flag,
                    data = subdat_vit_D_clean)

car::Anova(vit_d_supp_model_clean, type = "II")
```
